rationale: Verified: no *_test.go references the new counter. Real but small gap; metric registration is rarely unit-tested in this repo.
Correct: new helpers take `n` where siblings take `samples`. Pure naming asymmetry.
Commit-packaging advice riding on the real TotalSamples change; the underlying defect is reported elsewhere, this adds only hygiene.
States the defer-add behavior is correct and consistent with the sibling counter, which it is. No actionable content.
Hypothesis raised and cleared: the hoist is value-identical. Claim that something is fine, and it is fine.
Accurate that the restore is not deferred, but the panic is recovered in exec and the query already failed; no observable consequence.
JSON member order is not semantically significant; the cluster says so itself. Nothing to act on.
Naming/registration checked and found conformant. Restates that the code is correct.
True that the three attribution policies carry what-not-why comments; a documentation ask over code whose defects are reported separately.
Pre-existing AST mutation and defer, explicitly declared untouched and not a finding.
The default-step arm (`m[5m:]`) feeds the new subqStart/subqInterval consumers and is untested; a very common query shape with unverified stats.
Correct that evaluator start is mixed with stats Interval; they agree at every current call site, so this is latent fragility, not a defect.
Observes a test-only accessor mirrors an existing test-only accessor, and concludes it is fine. Correct and inert.
Confirms the max-samples contract is untouched by an observational counter. Accurate, no action.
The added `qs == nil` guard in InitStepTracking is indeed unreachable from both callers; dead defensive code, cosmetic.
Aliasing hypothesis raised and cleared; counts are taken before call(). Nothing for a maintainer to do.
The comment does say "disk reads" for data that may be in the head block; a wording nit in a comment.
Verified: smoothSeries calls matrixIterSlice with zero samplesStats increments, so smoothed selectors report samplesRead=0 for real reads.
Naming/help-text suggestion for two similarly named counters; reasonable but cosmetic once the counting defect is fixed.
Pre-existing vet notices, self-excluded from the verdict. No bearing on this change.
Confirmed: fullWindowCount is assigned only inside the recompute branch, so reused @-steps now record 0 where the old code counted the retained window.
Flags the shipped IMPLEMENTATION NOTES scratch block (and output-fitted goldens); the reviewer at that block says it shouldn't be here.
Attacks the same "steps after last outer" claim the reviewer questions at engine_test.go:1432; clamp is provably unreachable since tk <= endTimestamp.
Same point as the reviewer: GreaterOrEqual(SamplesRead, 0) passes even if the field is never populated.
Field ordering/alignment examined and dismissed; no padding cost, no linter enabled.
A public counter and always-present response field ship with disputed semantics and no gate; freezing them is a real maintainer decision.
Claims the SamplesRead=0 half of the reuse branch is intentional and correct, which it is.
Accurate asymmetry: scalar incremented unconditionally, per-step write silently skipped out of range. Latent only; no live divergence shown.
Early-out ordering checked; both counts are provably zero in that branch. Cleared hypothesis.
Nothing measures samplesRead against actual iterator yield, so the feature's core claim is unverified; a concrete, useful test proposal.
Wrong about structure: `### Query statistics` is a sibling of `### Range queries` under `## Expression queries`, and the #query-statistics anchor resolves.
Concludes the StepInvariantExpr accounting is correct as designed; a restatement of intended behavior.
Cutoff correctness investigated across many shapes and confirmed correct. Claim that code is fine, and it is.
Bare topic line about double registration; the collector is registered once and nothing asserts a defect.
Explicit no-finding on information disclosure; correct reasoning, nothing to act on.
Verifies peak/limit propagation is unchanged. Accurate confirmation, no defect.
Folding pre-window inner steps onto step 0 is the semantics the maintainer asks for, and the trailing clamp is unreachable, so the asserted fabrication does not hold.
countSamplesAfter adds a full scan of floats+histograms per step per series in the range-vector loop, ungated by the stats flag, replacing an O(1) len().
Verified: after truncation the code subtracts totalHPointSize(retained), not the dropped points, so currentSamples drifts. Pre-existing but real.
Correct: NewChild discards its receiver undocumented, now confusing next to a constructor that propagates the setting. Doc-comment nit.
Only hand-listed goldens are asserted; adding SamplesRead <= TotalSamples and SamplesRead == sum(perStep) would catch the double count.
Self-declared unverifiable residual risk that applies equally to the pre-existing field; not actionable here.
Monotonicity checked and confirmed; explicit no-finding.
States the change touches no concurrency primitives. True and inert.
The quotient is a step index bounded by the slice length, not a millisecond value; the claimed 2^31 ms negative truncation cannot occur.
Notes the query log picks up the field automatically; an observation with no action.
Confirmed 16 `New in` markers in the file and none on the new section; a small docs-convention gap.
Verified: AggregateExpr returns preprocessExprHelper(n.Expr) only, so Param is never preprocessed and step-invariance is judged on Expr alone. Pre-existing.
Accurate that the loop matches only MatrixSelector/SubqueryExpr, so a wrapped subquery arg is missed; pre-existing, consequence unverified.
Boundary hypothesis tested and refuted; the strict `>` is pinned by tests. Correct, no action.
Confirms both goldens were regenerated consistently; restates that the change is correct.
Checks whether the scalar/per-step divergence is live and concludes it is not. Cleared hypothesis.
Mutation probe showing the increment is test-pinned; a coverage observation, not a finding.
Real docs/behavior mismatch: samplesRead and both counters are unconditional, yet documented under the promql-per-step-stats flag heading.
Same substance as the reviewer at line 432: the index-by-index merge assumes a 1:1 child/parent step mapping that nothing guarantees or expresses.
Correct: the four new exported helpers get no direct unit tests; a modest coverage ask for a small stats package.
Verified that totalSize is taken after extendFloats injects two synthetic points, so the new read counter includes them; mirrors pre-existing TotalSamples behavior.
Correct API-shape asymmetry (method vs package function with opposite defaults) forcing the extra exported accessor. Style-level.
Panic hypothesis worked through and shown safe by truncating division. Claim that code is fine, and it is.
Confirms HPoint.size() is O(1) and folds the point into another finding. No independent content.
Mutation probe showing the delta branch is test-pinned; refutes a hypothesis rather than reporting one.
Nested-subquery blowup traced and found linear; explicitly folded into another finding.
States the new fields introduce no sharing; accurate and inert.
With per-step stats on, each subquery now allocates two []int64 sized by range/step from query text where NewChild allocated nothing.
Schema/golden consistency checked and found correct, including the absent `required` list.
Declares the ceiling-division attribution intentional and not an off-by-one; a cleared hypothesis.
Confirms the reuse branch cannot double count reads; correct and reported as a non-finding.
File placement judged consistent with the existing seam. No action implied.
Confirmed: `stats` is reassigned from the per-step-disabled run, so the PeakSamples-1 limit now derives from a value no assertion constrains.
Same point as the reviewer: the defaultEpsilon removal is unrelated churn that belongs in its own change.
Two divergent merge paths exist: the SubqueryExpr case reaches into another package's fields instead of the exported merge helper. Real layering problem.
The reviewer's "shouldn't this be 1 sample read?" on the `2 // subquery + outer` golden is exactly this double count of subquery reads.
True that the helper has no direct unit test; the cutoff is pinned indirectly, so the gap is a testing-hygiene ask.
Correct return-type asymmetry with totalHPointSize forcing one cast at the call site. Cosmetic.
Verifies the scalar counter is flag-invariant across both merge branches. Correct, non-actionable.
Checked that the UI does not consume samples stats; a negative result with nothing to do.
samplesRead is emitted in every stats response of a v1 API declared stable, so the contested counting semantics become hard to correct in 3.x.
"when" vs "if" in doc comments; accurate but below any reader's attention threshold.
Link and anchor style verified conformant; explicitly a non-violation.
Nil-guard hypothesis raised and dismissed as consistent with existing siblings. Cleared.
Division-by-zero raised and dismissed; Interval is non-zero whenever the per-step slices exist.
evalSeries charges a read per step per series, so a memoized sample re-returned under lookback is counted repeatedly — contradicting the field's documented I/O meaning.
The pre-existing metric's HELP was rewritten with a per-step-window claim that the @-reuse regression breaks; small, derivative of the counting defect.
Correct: the comment says "Subquery ran once" inside the StepInvariantExpr case, where the expression need not be a subquery. Comment-accuracy nit.
The "equals totalQueryableSamples for other query types" claim is false for step-invariant expressions — the diff's own goldens show 48 vs 12. Stated in four places.
Accurate: the new accessor returns nil on a second condition its doc omits and its sibling lacks. Test-only API, so impact is small.
Confirms the extraction is value-identical to the prior inline code. A cleared hypothesis.
Correct that four near-duplicate increment helpers now carry three different bounds disciplines; a consolidation/consistency point, no live failure.
Panic-reachability worked through and shown impossible. Claim that code is fine, and it is.
An uncovered nil-return branch with a concrete one-line fix in a test that already performs the needed run. Small but real.
Enumerates increment sites and confirms all are paired. A completeness check, not a finding.
Real but tiny: the new per-step description spells out flag gating that the pre-existing sibling description omits, so the two now disagree.
A broad enumeration of untested shapes for new code; legitimate but no demonstrated failure among them.
Verified: the new doc comment says only SamplesRead is merged, but UpdatePeakFromSubquery also propagates peak. Comment inaccuracy.
Correct: the exported getter returns EnablePerStepStats, not whether tracking was initialized, and carries no doc comment. Naming nit.
Underflow hypothesis proven impossible. Restates that the code is safe.
Correct: the length guard is unreachable at the only call site and untested — defensive code standing in for an unexpressed layout coupling.
Verified byte-identical triplicate cases; matches the reviewer's "a lot of these new tests seem very similar" at the head of that block.
Asserts a missing CHANGELOG entry, but the cluster's own check shows this repo edits CHANGELOG only at release cuts, so no convention is violated.
